html:
Copán is a Maya city in western Honduras, ruled by a dynasty founded in 426 and famous for its sculpture. Its Hieroglyphic Stairway carries the longest known Maya inscription.

Its founder, Kʼinich Yax Kʼukʼ Moʼ, had ties to the great city of Teotihuacan in central Mexico. Sixteen kings followed. They raised carved stone portraits, called stelae, in deep relief, and their scribes wrote dynastic history in Maya script.

In 738 the thirteenth king was captured and killed by Quiriguá, a former vassal. Copán recovered, but its valley was overfarmed, and the city declined in the Classic collapse after about 800. It is the best-known ancient site in Honduras and, with Tikal, one of the most studied of the Maya city-states.
sum: Copán is a Maya city in western Honduras, ruled by a dynasty founded in 426 and famous for its sculpture. Its Hieroglyphic Stairway carries the longest known Maya inscription.
